correctness.rationale: The directed bigram balance criterion is exactly the closed-walk zero-current condition. A Fourier trace counts those currents, a unique q-eigenvalue saddle yields a Gaussian local integral, and the exact cycle-Gram determinant q^(q-2) fixes the constant. Spectral Hessian verified independently numerically for q=3..6, exact determinant symbolically for q=3..7, direct enumeration and separate transfer counts agree on small cases. The proof treats every fixed q>=2 and all sufficiently large n; finite checks are not substituted for the limit proof.

value.rationale: The probability that all directed local pair statistics are invariant under reversal is a natural decoding/word-statistics invariant. The all-alphabet theorem gives a sharp structural transition from constant density at q=2 to polynomial rarity with exponent (q-1)(q-2)/4 and an explicit spanning-tree constant. This quantifies a fundamental local-word symmetry rather than an arbitrary small slice or a known finite table.
